A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same time-masked Transformer and DietCORP study on the Brain-to-Text ’24 benchmark. All pages, including figures, tables, equations, and appendices, are readable and support comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original decoding accuracy, computational measurements, ablations, robustness experiments, and test-time adaptation results.

after.justification: v2 reports original Transformer, DietCORP, ablation, input-overlap, and LLM fine-tuning experiments, alongside explicitly attributed baseline results.

M1.justification: The Transformer changes from seven blocks to five (v1 Section 4.3; v2 Section 3.5). More substantially, v2 adds an optional decoding stage that fine-tunes Llama 3.1 8B to merge transcripts from ten Transformer seeds (Section 4.2 and Appendix G). The central time-masking algorithm and single-step, patch-embedding-only DietCORP procedure remain.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same single-participant neural speech dataset and retain held-out-day evaluation. v2 removes the ventral-array-only, 64-channel scenario from v1 Section 5.3 and Figure 3a, narrowing coverage of reduced recording configurations. No new dataset, population, or decoding task is introduced.

E2.justification: v1’s attempted unidirectional Linderman GRU replication is replaced by an author-provided bidirectional Linderman result. v2 Table 1 adds reported comparisons against diphone decoding with a bidirectional GRU, including GPT 3.5 and Llama 3.1 70B merging configurations. Table 2 also adds a bidirectional GRU resource comparison, while the GRU-versus-Transformer held-out-day accuracy comparisons in v1 Figure 3 disappear.

E3.justification: Masked-model training changes from 600 to 250 epochs, the learning-rate drop moves from epoch 400 to 150, and DietCORP’s stated learning rate changes from 0.001 to 0.0005. Component ablations move from competition-test WER to validation WER, and masking sensitivity changes from validation PER to WER. New protocols cover LLM fine-tuning and non-overlapping GRU inputs. The reported training count also changes from 8,770 to 8,800; this alone does not establish a changed dataset.

E4.justification: v2 removes reduced-channel and reduced-training-data robustness experiments, masked-versus-unmasked loss curves, and the phoneme error breakdowns and confusion matrices. It adds non-overlapping-input and smaller-hidden-state GRU tests (Section 4.5), expands the masking-parameter sweep, and replaces the extended-training GRU control with a 250-epoch Transformer ablation. Component ablations and DietCORP augmentation sensitivity remain but are revised.

E5.justification: v2 explicitly specifies four ablation seeds and one LLM fine-tuning seed, and identifies beam-search timing uncertainty as standard deviation. It adds a one-sample test against the single-seed Linderman score and a two-sided test for input overlap. Existing ten-seed main comparisons and four-seed DietCORP reporting largely continue; increased replication of retained experiments is not established.

E6.justification: Transformer WER changes from 12.27% to 12.17% with the 3-gram setup and from 8.54% to 8.18% with the 5-gram setup. These are replacement results accompanying changed architecture and training settings, not controlled same-setting gains. v2 adds the 5.68% LLM-merging result and input-overlap findings. Resource tables change from 12.9M to 9.4M Transformer parameters and 3.33 to 2.66 GiB peak memory; adaptation, timing, and ablation results also change, while several robustness and error-analysis results are removed.

T1.justification: The relative-position attention equations, causal mask, beam-scoring formulas, and expected masking-fraction derivation remain mathematically unchanged. The derivation yielding approximately 53.44% masking moves from v1 Appendix I to v2 Appendix J. No new theorem, proof, or substantive formal assumption is introduced.

C1.justification: The three headline contributions remain time-masking, an efficient Transformer, and DietCORP. Their quantitative claims strengthen: the abstract changes parameter savings from 77% to 83%, peak-memory savings from 36% to 52%, and WER reduction from 19.5% to over 20%. These refine the existing accuracy-and-efficiency claims rather than redefine the central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 proposes patch-embedding normalization as an explanation for avoiding day-specific parameters and interprets the new overlap tests as supporting its efficiency argument. It adds a user-experience concern about revising decoded text, while removing the reduced-data robustness conclusion and extended-training limitation. The single-participant and approximately 60 GB language-model memory limitations were already present in v1.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a detailed LLM fine-tuning recipe, including QLoRA/Unsloth, the prompt, training order, and hyperparameters. It also provides explicit Linderman layer code, fuller model hyperparameter tables, WFST composition details, and a gradient-clipping value. Appendix H corrects the stated output rates from 20/25 Hz to 10/12.5 Hz, consistent with the retained output strides. The code-access link remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 refines its distinction from Chen et al. by explaining all-electrode versus electrode-specific patches and Swin attention. It adds references on end-to-end LLM neural decoding, unified streaming/non-streaming recognition, and the newly used models and software, while removing the Conformer and EcoTTA future-work references. The central positioning relative to GRUs, masking, and CORP remains.

P1.justification: The Results narrative is extensively rewritten and reordered around baseline comparisons, benchmark entries, DietCORP, ablations, and input overlap. v2 also revises the Discussion, repairs the Methods section hierarchy, moves references before the appendices, and replaces online/offline language-model terminology with explicit 3-gram/5-gram setup descriptions.

P2.justification: The visual presentation shifts substantially from plots toward tables: component ablations become a table, a consolidated benchmark-comparison table is added, and resource and hyperparameter tables are expanded or reorganized. Robustness plots and phoneme-error figures are removed. Figure 1 is updated, while the DietCORP plot is retained, revised, and relocated from Figure 4 to Figure 2.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reproducibility through fuller implementation details and makes the evidence more directly address the efficiency hypothesis through input-overlap tests and a matched-duration Transformer ablation. These gains are tempered by removal of reduced-data/channel robustness and phoneme-error analyses, and by the single-seed LLM result. The core contributions already had substantial support in v1, so the net improvement is limited rather than transformative.
